title: OpenAI collapses ChatGPT's Instant and Thinking modes into one GPT-5.6 Sol — and drops text-chat limits for free users
subtitle: The August 6 rollout gives Plus and Pro users a single reasoning-adjustable model with a slider replacing separate modes, and puts GPT-5.6 Luna on the Free tier with unlimited text chats subject only to abuse guardrails.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI on August 6 pushed the largest ChatGPT product change since the GPT-5 launch, rolling it out over the following days. For Plus and Pro subscribers, the previously separate GPT-5.6 Instant and GPT-5.6 Thinking configurations were merged into a single updated GPT-5.6 Sol experience, with a new slider that lets users dial reasoning effort up or down on a per-response basis instead of picking a mode in advance. OpenAI's own internal evaluation, published on the company's Deployment Safety Hub, put GPT-5.6 Sol at 68% fewer responses containing factual errors than GPT-5.5 Instant on a battery of financial, medical, and legal prompts requiring precise facts. For Free and Go users, GPT-5.6 Luna became the default model, unlimited text chats went live subject to what OpenAI calls 'abuse guardrails', and a new 'Think' button was added for higher-reasoning answers on harder questions. File uploads, image generation, and other tool calls remain metered.

The consumer play here is straightforward: unlimited free text chat closes the last major gap between ChatGPT's free tier and Google's free Gemini offering, which has run without per-message caps for months. The paid-tier play is more interesting. Collapsing Instant and Thinking into one model with an effort slider is an admission that the mode-picker was a UX failure — most users left it on the default and never touched it, which meant reasoning capability was rationed by whether people knew to switch. Moving the choice into the response, not the mode, means every conversation can now dip into deeper reasoning without a preflight decision. That matters commercially because reasoning-heavy queries are OpenAI's largest inference-cost line item, and the slider effectively lets the company push cheap defaults while advertising deep-reasoning access as always available.

The change lands into a market where competitors are moving the same way. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, released July 24, unified its extended-thinking mode into the default product surface. Google's Gemini 3.6 Flash, out July 21, was pitched around 'fewer wasted reasoning steps' for coding tasks. xAI's Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 shipped a similar collapse of speaking modes. The shared thesis across the frontier labs is that users neither want, nor should have to make, a routing decision every time they type — the model should route itself and the price surface should stay simple. Unlimited free access is the aggressive corollary: whichever consumer product owns default habit for the most people over the next six months owns the enterprise upsell that follows.

For learners: this is the phase of consumer AI where the pricing surface starts to matter more than the model card. If you are building on top of any hosted model, model the cost of your app against three scenarios — heavy free-tier substitution (users drop your product for the free chatbot), heavy reasoning-slider usage (your per-query cost quietly triples), and abuse-guardrail throttling (the vendor rate-limits you at exactly the wrong moment). None of those show up in a benchmark. All of them show up in a P&L. Read the fine print on the announcement pages you get excited about; the important lines are the ones about what the guardrails will and will not permit.
